enumeration.method: Search main pages 1-25 and independently enumerate bold Theorem headings from PDF font spans. The only printed environments are Theorem 4.2 on page 11 and Theorem 6.9 on page 20; neither spans a page boundary. Main references end on page 25, before the supplementary title on page 26.

checks: Both complete original theorem statements remain unchanged from the source-reviewed inventory, with its SHA-256 pinned by the final census.
PDF title, authors, arXiv stamp, page count and SHA-256 match the pinned provenance. Bold-heading enumeration independently confirms both printed theorem labels and their main-text pages.

Theorem 4.2 retains the complete scalar objective, nested supremum, indicator, root equation, saddle-solution assertion, risk formula and probability-scope sentence. The source root-star positions and nonnegative optimization domain are preserved.
Theorem 6.9 retains both positive-penalty objectives and the iff probability-limit conclusion. Its Phi_B formula lacks the absolute residual bars, as confirmed in the source crop.
All twelve interface records and eleven auxiliary source passages were reviewed against main-text pages. The activation residual coefficient square root and J matrix formula were checked visually.

The finalizer derives fourteen direct uses and fifteen related-theorem connections. A separate validator process accepts the original-statement handoff, graph, metrics, keywords, highlights and explanations.

Only the data model, random features and shifted activation are shared between the two theorem dependency closures. Theorem 4.2 does not acquire the event E_W, J, Gaussian surrogate features or proof-specific constraint sets.

Theorem 6.9 includes its explicit weight-matrix event and its section-wide dimensional limit convention. Its signal-normalization scope is recorded as a source limitation rather than silently importing Assumption 1(b).
The nested scalar optimization variables and both Phi quantities remain inline definitions in their original theorem records; no synthetic definition or proof theorem was substituted for them.

Every interface has literal natural-language source keywords, matching meaning-bearing selectors, and a source-backed explanation for every related theorem. Mathematical fragments have balanced braces.

source_notes: This census is specific to the February 2024 preprint, not an assertion of equality with the journal typesetting.
The theorem in the proof-outline section is included under the all-Theorems policy. Its supporting propositions, corollaries and lemmas are not separate theorem inventory entries.
The source uses a superscript epsilon for the robust ERM coefficient vector. It uses a superscript star for the scalar root definition and a subscript star for the root in the final risk formula.

The source limitations include Phi_B missing absolute-value bars, unspecified scalar boundary extensions, root-domain notation, signal-regime scope, and independence statements not explicitly supplied in the main-text definitions.
No supplementary definitions or proof content is used in the census. The main-text notice and title crop document the supplement boundary and its differently worded title.

unresolved_source_references.detail: The source is arXiv:2201.05149v2, stamped 1 February 2024. Title and authors match the corpus record. Equality with the published journal version is not established.

The attached supplement starts on PDF page 26 before the first appendix bookmark at page 27. Its title refers to classification accuracies although the main paper is about random-features regression. The notice on main page 22 uses that same supplement title. Supplementary definitions/proofs are excluded; introductory content exposed while checking the boundary is not used as census evidence.

Phi_A uses (|residual|+epsilon||J theta||)^2 but Phi_B prints (residual+epsilon||J theta||)^2 without absolute-value bars. The adjacent noisy-linear loss in Proposition 6.10 includes the bars. The theorem's asymmetric formulas are retained, not silently reconciled.

evidence.location: Theorem 4.2 root equation and risk formula (4.6)

unresolved_source_references.detail: Part (a) defines nu with a superscript star; (4.6) uses nu with a subscript star, without an explicit sentence equating that symbol to the root evaluated at the saddle point. That evaluation is the apparent intended reading, but original notation is preserved and the distinction is recorded.

The optimization domain permits zero alpha, beta, tau_g and tau_q, but the objective and root equation divide by these quantities. No boundary extension or extended-real convention is given in the inspected main-text statement. The domain is not silently restricted to strict positivity.

No domain for nu is stated in the root assertion. The objective multiplies a root-dependent term by an indicator threshold, but no separate definition is supplied for inactive branches or zero denominators. A nonnegative-root restriction or zero-root fallback is not added.

The source gives i.i.d. pairs, Gaussian x marginals and Gaussian xi marginals, but does not explicitly write xi independent of x in the model statement. Independent additive Gaussian noise is the conventional intended model; the missing explicit independence is recorded rather than inserted into the source quotation.

The surrogate Gaussian u is explicitly independent of x; its independence from response noise and W is not separately stated in the defining sentence. The sample uses one shared W. The audit does not replace the conditional-on-W interpretation with unconditional independence of all feature vectors.

Theorem 6.9 does not cite Assumption 1. Section 6 explicitly reiterates proportional n,d,N growth, but not the signal norm tending to one. The graph includes the repeated dimensional convention and records the unstated signal-regime scope; it does not silently impose the stronger normalization merely because the theorem is used to prove Theorem 4.2.

The printed assertion that sigma(w_i^T x) has unit variance conflicts with the shifted-ReLU definition. The Gaussian decomposition coefficients are retained as stated, and sigma is not replaced by its standardized nonlinear component.
The main text defines S by a complete real formula and refers to Lemma F.2 for further transform details. The appendix is not consulted and no additional convention from it is assumed.

The scalar beta in the saddle problem is distinct from the bold signal vector beta in data model (2.1). Scalar sigma squared in Theorem 4.2 is distinct from the activation function sigma. The scalar lambda inside the supremum of (4.5) is distinct from the positive regularization lambda in Theorem 6.9.

The limit c has no separately printed quantifier or range, and lambda,lambda_s,lambda_w are stated only to be positive. Treating c as a deterministic finite real limit and penalties as fixed is conventional context; the theorem does not explicitly describe a growing/diminishing penalty regime.

The general adversarial-risk definition uses max for an arbitrary predictive model and nonnegative loss, without general regularity guaranteeing attainment. The specialized shifted-ReLU squared loss is continuous on a compact perturbation ball. The robust ERM uses an argmin without a general tie-selection convention; no tie rule is invented.

ambient_resolution.shared: n is sample size, d the covariate dimension and N the number of random features. Bold W has shape N by d, its rows are w_l, and bold theta is an N-vector. The data-model signal bold beta is a d-vector. Standard primitives include Gaussian laws, sphere-uniform laws, Euclidean norms, inner products, matrix transpose, positive-semidefinite square root, Hadamard product, finite sums, expected loss, min/max/supremum and convergence in probability. A2 supplies the N-dimensional all-ones vector, A4 the matrix norm and indicator conventions. No library availability is asserted.
ambient_resolution.4.2: D1-D7 resolve all nonlocal objects. Tau squared is the noise marginal variance in (2.1), psi1 and psi2 come from Assumption 1, epsilon is the positive training radius and epsilon_test the separate test radius. Scalar sigma squared, the five saddle variables, their starred solution, the objective R and its lambda supremum are bound/defined inside the theorem. The ordinary error function erf is used without a main-text definition; its conventional real definition is 2/sqrt(pi) times the integral of exp(-t^2) from 0 to its argument. The root nu-star and the subscripted nu_star in the final formula are not silently identified; see source note. The limiting probability is expressly over both training data and W. Proof-only J, Gaussian surrogates, the event E_W, zeta penalties and constraint sets C_theta are not statement dependencies.
ambient_resolution.6.9: D1/D2/D3 supply data, W and the shifted activation. D8 is the explicitly assumed event E_W, D9 supplies J, and D11 supplies sample surrogate features f_i with coefficients D10. D12 supplies the reiterated dimensional limit convention. Phi_A and Phi_B are inline definitions, theta ranges over the N-dimensional coefficient space, lambda/lambda_s/lambda_w are inline positive parameters, bold1 is A2, and c is the common proposed limit. The theorem compares optimum values, not minimizers or risks. Its adjacent Proposition 6.10 and constraint set C_theta-prime are not imported as hypotheses.

review_limits: Source-fidelity and statement-dependency audit, not proof certification or mathematical repair.
Supplementary pages 26-86 excluded; the complete main-text formula for S is retained without reading its appendix reference.
